Reviewed at `ea950e5e` through the declared `review-pr` operation (#3035). Correctness lens, **0 findings**, converged at round 1 of 5. Judge spend $0.9580, one juror, session `28feaa50`.

**This lands the two defects that the apply-review-request path found in its own first hour of production**, and both are still missing from `main` as of this review — today's runs worked only because the executing copies were cherry-picked onto `ops/review-requests`.

The rename one is the live defect. The collector runs from main's checkout, so until this merges a push that git scores as a rename can return **zero files for a push whose request files are all new**, and the job exits green having applied nothing. That is the second silent-drop in this one function; the first was the genesis push, caught by review before it ever ran. Same shape both times: a verdict that never lands, with nothing anywhere saying so.

The dependency one is less dangerous because it fails **closed** — run `32248646760` collected all four requests correctly, failed every one at module resolution, and exited 1. Loud, and nothing partially applied. But main's workflow is the template the queue branch is recreated from, so it has to be right there too.

Recorded through the pipeline these two fixes protect.
